static_traits.name: Wei Jie
static_traits.educational_background: Doctorate in Veterinary Medicine (Doctorate in Veterinary Medicine)
static_traits.family_status: Grew up on a farm; older brother serves in the military; has two nephews
static_traits.social_status: Interactions with colleagues are tense due to lack of confidence; has a supportive network of friends and family, but has not shared the specific unease and self-doubt with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy experience; no similar psychological problems occurred before
static_traits.language_features: Clear and organized expression; cooperation acceptable but with a skeptical attitude; tends toward negative self-evaluation and repeated self-negation

basic_info.main_problem: I believe my background growing up on a farm limits my success outside agriculture, leading to self-doubt and lack of motivation, gradually affecting my daily confidence and job satisfaction, especially intensifying when facing work challenges.
basic_info.core_demands: Realized that these beliefs are hindering my personal and professional growth, and therefore decided to seek counseling at this time.
growth_experiences: Grew up on a farm from childhood, with the family mainly in agriculture; the elder brother serves in the military, and there are two nephews. This upbringing gradually formed a cognitive frame that 'origin and background determine career prospects'.

As an adult, when choosing to switch from agriculture to becoming a veterinarian (a career outside agriculture), the client's original beliefs about background conflicted with the new career path, and persistent self-doubt and stress began to appear; these feelings intensified markedly when encountering challenges in non-agricultural professional environments.

core_beliefs: My background (growing up on a farm) determines that I cannot succeed outside agriculture

special_situations.event: At work receiving a complex case, feeling 'completely lost'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perform perfectly in front of complex cases, it proves I am not good enough, and my farm background makes me lack the ability to succeed outside agriculture
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated self-doubt, trying to ignore and suppress these thoughts to continue working
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not good enough; I should not have left the farm

special_situations.event: A colleague invites one to comment on a treatment plan
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot immediately give a perfect and authoritative answer, others will think I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Giving evasive answers, avoiding direct communication with colleagues
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will find out I am a fraud; I do not belong here

special_situations.event: Constantly facing challenges and pressure in daily work in non-agricultural fields
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I leave agriculture, I am doomed not to succeed; facing challenges means I will ultimately fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowering expectations, lacking motivation, trying hard to avoid being asked to take on higher responsibility
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am doomed not to succeed; sooner or later this will prove I am incapable

special_situations.event: Daily interactions with colleagues are tense due to insufficient confidence
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not perform well enough when colleagues interact with me, it means the strained relationship is caused by my incompetence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces social contact and tries to avoid evaluative situations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They can see through my incompetence; it is all my problem

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and achieve success and belonging in a career outside agriculture
core_conflict.fear: Fears being seen through as a 'fraud' who is not good enough / incompetent, worrying about being negated and excluded by others
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being judged and failing by avoidance, lowering exposure, and maintaining distance, preserving a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough outsider / an 'impostor' who may be exposed
object_relations.object_representation: Picky others who will judge and can 'see through' oneself (such as colleagues)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests identifying and testing automatic thoughts and conducting reality testing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes these methods 'may not work' for them and that change is hard to achieve, thereby reducing participation and expectations (denial of change)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in a skeptical and reserved tone, using expressions such as 'this may not help' and 'I do not think it will change', avoiding going into details and emotions, and keeping the topic on the surface as much as possible.

manifestations: Decreased job satisfaction, difficulty gaining pleasure in work and life
Persistent self-doubt and lack of motivation weaken the sense of meaning in career pursuits
Avoids interacting with colleagues for fear of being seen through or judged
Unwilling to share specific unease and doubts with supportive family and friends
outcomes: 主观疏离与Increased sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and self-reproach, involving excessive self-restriction and caution, and is overly careful about contact.
manifestations: Repeatedly expresses doubt and low expectations in counseling (such as 'I do not think this will change anything')
Frequently second-guessing one's actions and decisions, worrying about being seen through as incompetent

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: In interactions, presumes others will think they are a fraud / incompetent (mind-reading inference)
Reducing direct contact out of worry about others' evaluations

positive_force: Having a doctorate in veterinary medicine and professional training background
Loves animals; has intrinsic motivation supporting the career choice
Having a support network of family and friends (close relationship with elder brother)
Has handled similar cases before and has some practical experience
negative_force: Rigid self-labeling and overgeneralization (equating background with ability and future)
Excessive worry about others' evaluation caused by mind reading and fortune telling
A coping pattern of avoiding colleague interaction and giving vague answers
Persistent self-doubt and insufficient motivation, affecting job satisfaction and self-care

target_behavior.behavior: When colleagues ask for professional opinions, giving vague answers and avoiding interaction
antecedent: A colleague asks one to give an opinion on a treatment plan
Needing to express professional judgment in team communication
target_behavior.core_reason: Regards the farm upbringing background as a limitation, labels the self as 'incompetent / not good enough', and worries about being seen through and judged
target_behavior.function: Escaping being evaluated and potential failure, reducing anxiety and shame in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Strained interpersonal relationships, impaired teamwork, further decline in self-evaluation

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent anxiety and self-doubt at work (negative self-thinking cycle)
antecedent: Facing complex cases and high-difficulty tasks
Encounters challenges and pressure in a non-agricultural work environment
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'origin determines success or failure' is activated and overgeneralized to all current challenges, producing self-negation and expectations of failure
target_behavior.function: Reduces in the short term the tension brought by uncertainty through self-defense (lowering expectations, avoidance)
target_behavior.consequence: Motivation declines, job satisfaction decreases, daily self-care is difficult, and career development is restricted
